title: Morgan Stanley China CEO: Chinese market lacks diversity
description: Morgan Stanley China CEO Wei Christianson on the state of the Chinese market and economy.

asr.full_text: The worry of China's economic slowdown hitting markets around the world. Maria sat down with Morgan Stanley, China CEO, Wei Christiansen to get her take on the Chinese markets today. I think it's important for people to remember that China in absolute terms is a 10.4 trillion economy. So even though people are focused on a precise growth whether it is 5% , 6% or 7% in absolute number for instance in case of a 5% growth that's really a low end scenario we are still talking about $500 billion economic growth which is roughly about 40% of the worldís growth. Let me ask you about the governmentís steps recently to stop and halt the selloff that weíve seen. I think thatís what worries market participants as well. You see the Chinese stock market go down sharply and all of a sudden the government steps in and says, ìOK, we're halting things and we're telling short-sellers they can't do that anymore. How do you deal with that, running Morgan Stanley China? I mean this has to be hard to take. MINGZHE CHUNG, Well, this measure that the Chinese government have introduced is what we call the circuit breaker. Essentially, it uses the CSI 300 as a benchmark so if it goes down by five percent will cause for 15 minutes to a stop and that if seven percent then the whole day's suspension this was not a Chinese invention this was actually invented in the United States in 1987 I was just going to say, we know that the New York Stock Exchange used to do things like this Yes so that that was about 30 years ago. I think it's important to recognize that when governments, or any government, put together a regulatory framework, there's no or fit at all kind of a model, right? It works in the US, and it works in certain markets, but it may not necessarily fit other markets or other jurisdictions. Why are we seeing such a reaction on the part of investors? Why does the market keep selling off in your view? I think there was ... last year the market was rough, and the government intervened. And again it's all these unknown factors factors and the investors were not clear about what was lying ahead. And also, I think it reflects the structural issues of the market. This market likes diversity in terms of the investor basis because 80% of the trading of the Chinese market is retail. Averse to the United States, it's two-thirds of the trading as institution. I think the homogeneous base of the investor base actually is not very healthy. Because it lacks the differences in valuation, and it deters other investors to participate. ATHER, I WAS GOING TO ASK YOU ABOUT THE CHINESE INVESTOR TODAY. ARE YOU SEEING A CHANGE IN TERMS OF THE MENTALITY THAT INCREASINGLY WANT TO PUT MONEY INTO THE PUBLIC MARKETS OR IS THIS MAJOR SELL-OFF NOW BECAUSE IT'S NOT GOING TO LOWER THAT I THINK? investor today are you seeing a change in terms of the mentality batting increasing leave want to put money into the public markets or is this major cell of now so shutting that down I think it there is still a lot of the amendment was speculation in the marketplace all times it is really important I for the garment to really at diversified investor-based and also the products and the instruments right I it needs to be diverse should be able to diversify the investor base. And also, the product is instrument, it needs to be diversified. The other issues are the quality of the information disclosure. I think the Chinese regulators are going to introduce a registration-based system, which hopefully will enhance disclosure standards because investors needs to have access to truthful and fully discolored information in order to assess the valuation to reflect the fundamentals of the company. As we wrap up here Wei, earlier in the interview as we were talking about the economy you put it into context in terms of the size of the Chinese economy, how would you characterize the growth story today? Is it weaker than many people think? I think actually the growth has slowed down, there's no doubt about it. But the good news is that you have a better mix. In other words the Chinese government has been focusing on rebalancing, meaning, you know, simultaneously they are trying to change the growth driver from the investment-driven into to the consumption and the service-driven, which is good. And at the same time they need to address the structural issues and the problems that exist in the system. And also, they are taking care of the supply side of the reform, which means they are taking care of overcapacity, and which has been build up in the past few years, because of the stimulus policies that have been introduced for many years. Special thanks to Wei Christensen, there.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it is framed as a televised interview about China's market and economy, with a Morgan Stanley China executive discussing market topics rather than presenting a viewer-directed offer. The transcript centers on market structure, disclosure standards, investor access to information, and the slowing growth outlook, although sparse sampling and possible ASR inaccuracies limit assessment of portions not shown or clearly transcribed.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary subject is financial news and market analysis concerning Chinese market structure, regulation, investor participation and economic growth.
